questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The most popular baby names in the UK today
How parents should choose a name for their child
A writer whose names tell her family's story
Why people change their names when they marry
questions.why: They meet Sheela Banerjee, whose name combines her English and Indian identity and family history.

questions.q: What does Beth say happens when someone shouts your name in the street?
options: You feel embarrassed
You turn to look without thinking
You pretend not to hear
You shout back
questions.why: Beth says if you hear someone shout your name, you automatically turn to look.

questions.q: Where did Sheela's parents come from?
options: Bengal, in east India
Hayes, in West London
The south of India
Pakistan
questions.why: She was born in Hayes to parents from the east Indian state of Bengal.

questions.q: Why did Sheela's parents give her a typical English first name?
options: It was easier to spell
It was her grandmother's name
They wanted to hide their Indian roots
They wanted her to feel safe in London
questions.why: Neil says her parents wanted their daughter to feel safe in London.

questions.q: What led Sheela to investigate her family story?
options: She wanted to understand her culture more
Her parents asked her to write a book
Her teacher gave her a school project
She wanted to change her name
questions.why: Beth says, wanting to find out more about her culture, Sheela started to pull the threads behind her family story.

questions.q: What happened to Sheela's original surname?
options: Her parents shortened it when they moved to London
The British changed it, not wanting to say it
She changed it herself to sound more English
It was changed when her family changed caste
questions.why: She says the British changed 'Bandyopadhyay' because they couldn't be bothered to pronounce it, or couldn't.

questions.q: How does Sheela feel about the name Banerjee?
options: Proud, because it shows her high caste
Happy, because it's easy for English people to say
Mixed, because it is a reminder of colonial rule
Angry, and she plans to change it
questions.why: She says it's a very mixed name because it shows they were colonial subjects, so it's tricky to carry around.

options: That Sheela doesn't look or sound very English
That most Indian names are now anglicised
That Sheela's book is mostly about politics
That the Empire's capital became home to migrants
questions.why: She says ironically London, capital of the British Empire, became the destination for migrants from all over the world.
